incoming_learnings: Before funding pool preparation with food, establish a public, admissible identification or unknown-potion test plan, including inventory protection and a budgeted chest return trip. A meal is not proof that testing or retrieval becomes possible. Keep the chest pending until collection is verified.

review.review: The Mage died during the Goo fight. The initiating problem was an unfavorable engagement on healing water, before the withdrawal-budget failures: decisions 1460–1464 traded melee blows while four staff charges remained, and decisions 1469–1470 reduced hero health from 27 to 12. The full selector chain explains this: Goo first seeks an admitted immediate dry lure, then chooses the highest estimated attack; the inspected staff scores slightly higher in melee while the hero is healthy. Public bar increases corroborate water healing. Decision 1481 begins exhausted-magic withdrawal; later fallback retreats do not demonstrate a stopped clock or a safe alternative. Accepted terminal transitions at lines 4356 and 4360 show health falling from four to one to zero. The final damage source is not established. No policy memory was reconstructed and no counterfactual gameplay was executed. Source browsing resolved the selection-chain gap but did not establish a focused deterministic defect or an admitted replacement, so no patch or new regression is supplied. Existing tests pass: 1,569 tests, four skipped. Post-death potion identities were not treated as pre-death knowledge.
review.learnings: Investigate the water engagement before extending withdrawal or preparation limits. Establish a publicly supported dry approach or attack/resource plan that preserves charge-warning escape and health/hunger budgets. Do not infer a safe potion from its later revealed identity, and keep mandatory progression loot pending until collection is verified.
